'''Bigambul''' (also ''Bigambal'', ''Bigumbil'', ''Pikambul'', or ''Pikumbul'') is an [[extinct language|extinct]] and unclassified [[Australian Aboriginal languages|Australian Aboriginal language]] from the [[Pama–Nyungan languages|Pama–Nyungan language family]].<ref name="AIATSIS" /> The Bigambul language region includes the landscape within the local government boundaries of the [[Goondiwindi Region|Goondiwindi Regional Council]], including the towns of [[Goondiwindi]], Yelarbon and [[Texas, Queensland|Texas]] extending north towards [[Moonie, Queensland|Moonie]] and [[Millmerran, Queensland|Millmerran]].<ref name=":43">{{SLQ-CC-BY|url=https://maps.slq.qld.gov.au/iyil/view/4?embed=true|title=Bigambul|publisher=[[State Library of Queensland]]|website=Queensland Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages map|url-status=live|accessdate=25 May 2022}}</ref> The AUSTLANG database maintained by the Australian Institute of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Studies states that the Bigambul language was spoken by the [[Bigambul|Bigambul people]], with [[Gambuwal language|Gambuwal]] and [[Kwiambal language|Kwiambal]] (or Gujambal) known dialects.<ref name="AIATSIS" /> However, it is likely that the [[Gamilaraay language|Gamilaraay]] (or Yuwaaliyaay) language was used by those peoples living in southern Bigambul territory.<ref name=":NSWDoAA">{{cite web |date=14 May 2012 |title=Map of NSW Aboriginal Languages |url=http://www.alrrc.nsw.gov.au/default.aspx?nav_id=32 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120327063707/http://www.alrrc.nsw.gov.au/default.aspx?nav_id=32 |archive-date=27 March 2012 |access-date=14 May 2012 |publisher=New South Wales Department of Aboriginal Affairs}}</ref>

== Classification ==
Dixon (2002)<ref name=":dixon2002">{{cite book |last=Dixon |first=R. M. W. |url=http://www.cambridge.org/catalogue/catalogue.asp?isbn=0521473780 |title=Australian Languages: their nature and development |publisher=Cambridge University Press |year=2002 |author-link=R. M. W. Dixon}}</ref> groups Bigambul together with the [[Yugambeh–Bundjalung languages|Bundjalung languages]] while O'Grady, Voegelin and Voegelin classify it as a [[Wiradhuric languages|Wiradjuric language]].<ref name=":wafer2008">{{cite book |last1=Wafer |first1=Jim |title=A Handbook of Aboriginal Languages of New South Wales and the Australian Capital Territory |last2=Lissarrague |first2=Amanda |publisher=Muurrbay Aboriginal Language & Culture Co-operative |year=2008}}</ref>{{rp|333}}

[[Glottolog]] states that Wafer and Lissarrague (2008)<ref name=":wafer2008" />{{rp|332–340}} have classed Bigambul, [[Guyambal language|Guyambal]] and [[Yugambal language|Yugambal]] together.<ref>{{cite web |year=2020 |title=Bigambal |url=https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/biga1237 |work=[[Glottolog]] 4.3 |editor-last1=Hammarström |editor-first1=Harald |editor-last2=Forkel |editor-first2=Robert |editor-last3=Haspelmath |editor-first3=Martin |editor-last4=Bank |editor-first4=Sebastian}}</ref>

== Vocabulary ==
Some words from the Bigambul language, as spelt and written by Bigambul authors, include:<ref name=":43" />

* ''Bamburr'': kangaroo
* ''Dhigaraa'': bird
* ''Dhimba'': snake
* ''Dhurrii'': land
* ''Gayker'': echidna
* ''Gillee'': sun
* ''Gool'': fish
* ''Gulli'': rain/water
* ''Koobee'': possum
* ''Noorah'': home/camp
* ''Warril'': river
* ''Weeimba gilee'': hello
* ''Woodyun'': grass
